name: Moab · Arches & Canyonlands
tagline: Two national parks, one red-rock base
summary: Give Arches and Canyonlands separate days. Add Dead Horse Point at sunset if you still have daylight and energy, rather than trying to hike everything in one day.
seasonNote: Summer heat is severe on exposed rock; spring/fall are more comfortable. Winter ice can still make trails hazardous.
arrival: Drive from Grand Junction, Salt Lake City or another Utah base; CNY flights are limited.
gettingAround: A car is usually needed; book appropriate guided trips for remote roads rather than taking a standard rental off-road.
cashTip: Cards work in town; carry an emergency reserve. Daily budget excludes car/fuel and park admission; Arches/Canyonlands do not appear in the designated 11-park 2026 nonresident-fee list.
foodTip: Buy a substantial picnic and refill water before entering either park.
buyTip: Pick up maps, sun protection and locally made desert art; leave rocks and cultural objects in place.
baseArea: Moab town for services and restaurant choice.

connections.note: Approximate direct drive; allow extra nights for the scenic Utah parks route.
Approximate direct road journey; Monument Valley is an optional separate stop.

reviewSummary: Visitor lists foreground Arches, Canyonlands and Dead Horse Point. The latter has a Travellers’ Choice badge in the retrieved listing, supporting it as a strong third landscape stop.

items.name: Delicate Arch hike
items.summary: The signature freestanding arch rewards a sustained exposed hike.
items.expect: Heat, slickrock and uneven ledges; the hike is different from the distant viewpoint.
items.tip: Carry water, start early and check weather. Arches does not require timed-entry reservations in 2026.
items.priceNote: Arches base fee is up to USD 30 per private vehicle; other Arches stops share that admission. Valid passes may apply.

review.note: Exact attraction listing snapshot; review volume is not visitor count.

whyVisit: The freestanding arch stands apart from the surrounding slickrock bowl.
Reaching it on foot gives a close view quite different from the distant roadside viewpoint.
visitFlow: Start with water and a suitable weather window.
Follow the marked trail, treating ledges and the return journey seriously.
items.tradeoffs: Heat, slickrock and uneven ledges; the hike is different from the distant viewpoint.

items.name: The Windows & Double Arch
items.summary: Shorter walks reveal several major rock formations.
items.expect: Busy parking areas and sun-exposed trails.
items.tip: A useful alternative to a longer hike; arrive early and stay on marked paths.
items.priceNote: Included with Arches admission or a valid qualifying pass.

review.note: Exact attraction listing snapshot; review volume is not visitor count.

whyVisit: Several major arches sit within a relatively compact trail area.
Shorter walks make the cluster useful for travellers avoiding the longer Delicate Arch hike.
visitFlow: Arrive early for the parking area.
Walk to the Windows and Double Arch on their signed paths.
items.tradeoffs: Busy parking areas and sun-exposed trails.

items.name: Canyonlands: Island in the Sky
items.wiki: Island in the Sky (Canyonlands National Park)
items.summary: Mesa-top overlooks reveal the vast canyon landscape.
items.expect: A separate park day; the Needles district is not a quick adjacent stop.
items.tip: Choose a few overlooks and one short trail; carry water as services are sparse.
items.priceNote: Planning allowance for separate Canyonlands private-vehicle admission; qualifying pass may cover it.

review.note: Exact attraction listing snapshot; review volume is not visitor count.

whyVisit: Mesa-top overlooks expose the scale of the canyon systems below.
The district offers a broad landscape view distinct from close-up arch walks.
visitFlow: Choose a few overlooks and one suitable short trail.
Drive between them with water and a realistic return time.
items.tradeoffs: A separate park day; the Needles district is not a quick adjacent stop.

items.name: Mesa Arch
items.summary: A short trail reaches a natural frame over the canyon.
items.expect: Sunrise photography can be crowded; cliff edges are unprotected.
items.tip: A later morning visit can be calmer; never climb the arch.
items.priceNote: Included with Canyonlands admission or a valid qualifying pass.

review.note: Exact attraction listing snapshot; review volume is not visitor count.

whyVisit: The arch frames a deep canyon view from a short trail.
Changing light alters the rock and the landscape beyond it.
visitFlow: Walk the signed trail without rushing for a photograph.
View the arch from the permitted ground and stay back from the cliff edge.
items.tradeoffs: Sunrise photography can be crowded; cliff edges are unprotected.

items.name: Dead Horse Point

items.tradeoffs: A separate Utah state park, not covered by the federal annual pass.

dayClusters.label: Arches: the main formations
dayClusters.note: Prepare supplies first, then group the Arches stops within one park day. The Delicate Arch hike is strenuous in heat; substitute its distant viewpoint if needed and avoid treating all time estimates as queue-free.

dayClusters.label: Canyonlands Island in the Sky, including Mesa Arch
dayClusters.note: Mesa Arch is a stop within the Island in the Sky day, not another trip to Canyonlands. The broad park duration already allows several viewpoints; trim them to fit daylight and avoid double-counting that time.

dayClusters.label: Dead Horse Point and town preparation
dayClusters.note: Browse or replace gear in town, then drive to the state-park overlooks later in the day. Its admission is separate from federal park passes; allow time for the return drive.
